findings.description: The entire evidential basis of this record lies outside the distribution, so no reader of this repository can re-derive any of its numbers. FB2-REV-FND-000042 is severity high and disposition accepted - an OPEN finding - and every headline figure it states comes from three files under docs/artifacts/.work/: verification-env/sil/tools/find_vacuous_tests.py, verification-env/sil/logs/vacuous-final.json and verification-env/sil/VACUOUS-TESTS.md. That whole subtree is excluded from distribution and from the record population, three ways, all measured: 'git check-ignore -v docs/artifacts/.work' reports 'docs/artifacts/.gitignore:2:.work/'; 'git ls-files docs/artifacts/.work' returns ZERO tracked files; and corpus.py's iter_corpus_artifacts skips any path with '.work' in its parts, with a docstring saying evaluator-only is 'deliberately kept out of the record population'. docs/artifacts/.gitignore's own first line reads 'Temporary/local-only files excluded from distribution'. So on a clean checkout the cited files do not exist and the claims '82 of the 313 test files are vacuous', 'of the green files, 53 assert nothing and 192 carry a real assertion', '30 of those are build failures', 'the asserting count ROSE from 175 to 192', 'the vacuous green count also rose from 47 to 53' and '6 of the 23 tests that newly went from build failure to pass are themselves vacuous' are unverifiable - and unverifiable in the strict sense that the instrument that produced them is not in the repository either. This is not a new failure mode for this corpus; it is one it has already been bitten by and fixed once, and its own .gitignore records the precedent at length: 'A citation that names a file the distribution does not contain is a checkable claim that is false on a clean checkout: corpus.py check failed there with 14 evidence_file_missing findings that this working tree cannot reproduce, because the files were present' - fixed by re-including the logs rather than by rewriting the citation. THAT FIX DID NOT REACH THIS CASE, and the reason is structural rather than an oversight: the fix works because execution records carry citations in evidence_files[], which corpus.py checks for existence. Finding records have no such slot. Measured across the whole family: 0 of 42 finding records carry evidence_files and 0 carry source_anchors, so every path a finding record cites is free text that no tool resolves. The corpus therefore cannot detect this class of error in a finding record even in principle, which is why it survived. The finding's own reasoning, its reading rule and its framing are careful and were NOT disturbed by this review; only its citability is defective. NOT CORRECTED HERE: no finding record was modified, and re-including .work/ is a repository-distribution decision, not a documentation fix.

findings.description: Three records in this family file a block under the key 'reverification' that contains no re-verification. In 39 of the 42 finding records that block carries seven keys - date, method, audit_class, condition_still_holds, disposition_before, revision_before, evidence - and it is the corpus's proof-of-currency mechanism: a reader asks 'does this condition still hold?' and reads condition_still_holds, with audit_class to classify it and evidence to see the re-derivation. FB2-REV-FND-000039, FB2-REV-FND-000041 and FB2-REV-FND-000042 instead carry only date, method and 'raised_by': 'finding-closure pass over the 38 pre-existing records'. That is a provenance stamp of when the finding was RAISED, filed under the key the other 39 use for whether it is still TRUE. No condition_still_holds, no audit_class, no evidence, no disposition_before, no revision_before. The consequence is specific: a machine that decides currency by reading reverification.condition_still_holds finds the key absent on these three rather than false, and must special-case them; a human who assumes the key means the same thing in all 42 records reads 'raised_by' as if it were a verdict. The three affected records are not a random subset - they include two of the four severity-high records that remain OPEN (000041 and 000042, both disposition 'accepted'), and the one high record closed in this pass's own subject area (000039). THIS REVIEW DID THE MISSING WORK AND RECORDS THE RESULT, so the cost of the gap is visible rather than merely asserted. FB2-REV-FND-000041's substance was re-derived here and it HOLDS on every checkable claim: FB2-VER-TMS-000016..000020 exist with oracle_detail.kind of source_grounded, analytical_model, source_grounded, source_grounded and synthetic_assumption respectively, exactly as the record states; FB2-VER-EXE-000016..000020 all carry execution_kind 'none', outcome 'blocked' and a blocked_reason; all five FB2-SAF-SEC-* requirements carry verification_status 'not_verified' and a real_source_presence block; FB2-SAF-TAR-000001 exists and its own text describes the requirements as forward-engineered for a hypothetical project. FB2-REV-FND-000039's substance also holds: the '-FSR-' id filter is absent from the safety_requirement_completeness_checker in corpus.py, which now selects on declared type and declared domain, and the four self-tests that pin the widened scope (t_fault_reaction_rule_covers_sec_requirements, _still_covers_fsr_requirements, _respects_domain_boundary, _silent_when_field_present) are present in cmd_selftest. So the defect is in the meta-fields, not in the content - which is exactly why it is medium and not high, and why it is recorded against the records' own key rather than against their conclusions.

findings.description: Seven records state their own disposition wrongly, in a field that now contradicts the field that carries it. FB2-REV-FND-000023 through FB2-REV-FND-000029 are all dispositioned 'resolved'. The lifecycle_status_note on each of the seven nonetheless ends: 'The disposition stays \'accepted\' because this schema has no closed value and the finding was valid: the acceptance stands and the closure is recorded in the resolution and revision history.' Two sentences are now false in all seven: the disposition does not stay 'accepted', it is 'resolved', and this schema does have a closed value - finding.schema.json's disposition enum carries 'resolved', with a normative definition in docs/artifacts/governance/finding-disposition-vocabulary.md. That is the same migration the seven records themselves record: the disposition_note of the records that DID migrate says so explicitly ('It was \'accepted\' before this revision, and that word was ambiguous'), and the sibling record FB2-REV-FND-000022 records the same migration in its resolution ('RESOLVED, and the vocabulary member is corrected... migrated to it'). So the seven were migrated in the disposition field and the explanatory note was left describing the pre-migration state. A reader who takes the note for the field learns that these seven are open acknowledgements, which is the precise confusion the migration was made to remove - 'accepted' was carrying at least three different jobs across this corpus... which left a reader unable to tell a closed finding from an open one by machine'. LOW AND NOT HIGHER, for three stated reasons: the machine-readable field is the correct one and the contradiction is in prose; no verdict, no severity and no evidence is affected; and a reader who reads the disposition field, which is what every tool in this corpus reads, gets the right answer. Recorded rather than corrected: these seven records were not modified by this pass.
findings.evidence: Read from the records. The 33 draft findings and the migrated records FB2-REV-FND-000001 to -000022 all state the migration in their own notes, so the seven are the only records where the note and the field disagree. 7 of 42 records affected; 35 of 42 clean.
